newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Multipolar denies stake sale talks.
newsitem.headline: Multipolar denies stake sale talks.

text.p: Indonesia's Multipolar Corp said on Friday it was not holding talks with local businessman Hari Darmawan over the possible sale of a stake in the firm.
Darmawan, founder of retailer Matahari Putra Prima, had been quoted by a local newspaper as saying he planned to take a stake in the Multipolar, part of the Lippo Group.
The proposed move came after Multipolar recently took a 50.1 percent controlling interest in Matahari.

"There is no discussion of Multipolar stake purchase between our company and Hari Darmawan, except that on several occasions he has expresed his interest in investing in Multipolar through the stock exchange," Multipolar's president director Winardi Setiaputra said in the statement answering Reuters' questions.
Winardi said Multipolar would welcome Darmawan as a significant investor in the company, under such circumstances, as it believed he could make a positive contribution to the firm.
But he said Darmawan's own plan to invest in Multipolar was not a part of the agreement that saw Multipolar take control of Matahari.
